results.title: Tokenising government securities could attract more foreign investors to Ghana – WeWire CEO
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of WeWire, Ebenezer Ghanney, says tokenising Ghana's government securities could make it easier for international investors to access the domestic market and expand the government's sources of funding. He believes issuing digital tokens linked to government bonds and Treasury instruments could reduce some of the traditional barriers that make it difficult for foreign investors to participate in Ghana's financial market. Speaking at the Africa Virtual Assets Summit (AVSA) in Accra, Mr Ghanney identified government securities as among the financial products that could be relatively easy to tokenise because existing market structures and custody arrangements are already in place. “Government securities are easier because the product doesn't require heavy lifting like gold. With gold, we need to make sure that we have the custody sorted out,” he said.

results.title: Before buying AI, businesses need to ask better questions
results.content: A recent analysis encouraged Ghanaian entrepreneurs to connect artificial intelligence with practical needs, including customer communication and record-keeping. That is a useful starting point, but it leaves another question: how should a business choose the company providing the technology? A convincing demonstration should begin a discussion, not end it. Before committing money or uploading customer information, owners need to understand what a service delivers, what remains their responsibility, and how they can leave if it disappoints. Request a Demonstration of Your Actual Work Consider a hypothetical printing business in Kumasi comparing two services for preparing quotations. Instead of accepting a supplier's polished examples, the owner could provide a fictional order and an approved price list.
